subject: Why is my code using so much memory ?

messages.author: f57f5660bf9ee268
messages.subject: Why is my code using so much memory ?
parts:
Hello, I apologize in advance if my question is naive or if my code is not well-written. I am quite new to STAN. For practical reasons, I copy-paste my code below :

functions{
  vector compute_delta(vector delta_d, matrix Kxd, matrix invKd){
    return Kxd*(invKd*append_row(rep_vector(0,1),delta_d));
  }
 
  matrix compute_A(vector c, int Ns, int Ndim){
    vector[Ndim] E1;
    vector[Ndim] O;
    vector[Ndim] E;
    matrix[Ndim,Ns] A;
    vector[Ndim] auxA;
    vector[Ndim] auxA2;
    O = rep_vector(1, Ndim);
    E1 = rep_vector(0, Ndim);
    E1[1] = 1;
    auxA = O + sqrt(Ndim)*E1;
    for (l in 1:Ns){
      auxA2 = rep_vector(0,Ndim);
      A[,l] = rep_vector(0,Ndim);
      for (k in 1:(Ndim-1)){
        E = rep_vector(0,Ndim);
        E[k+1] = 1;
        auxA2 = auxA2 + c[k+(l-1)*(Ndim-1)]*(E - (2*(to_row_vector(auxA)*E)/(to_row_vector(auxA)*auxA))*O - (2*sqrt(Ndim)*(to_row_vector(auxA)*E)/(to_row_vector(auxA)*auxA))*E1);
      }
      A[,l] = auxA2;
    }
    return A;
  }
 }

data{
  int<lower=1> p;
  int<lower=1> Ndim;
  int<lower=1> K;
  int<lower=2> Nc;
  int<lower=1> Ns;
  real t[K];
  vector[Ndim] y[K];
  int<lower=1> group[K];
  matrix[Nc,Nc] invKd;
  matrix[Ndim,Nc] Kxd;
}

parameters{
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
  real<lower=0> sigma_tau;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
  // Random effects
  real<lower=0> p0;
  real<lower=0> t0;
  real<lower=0> xi_barre;
  vector[Nc-1] delta_d;
  vector[(Ndim-1)*Ns] c;
  vector[p] alpha_raw;
  vector[p] tau_raw;
  vector[Ns] s[p];
}

transformed parameters{
  vector[Ndim] mu[K];
  vector[p] tau;
  vector<lower=0>[p] alpha;
  // Non-centered parametrization
  tau = t0 + sigma_tau*tau_raw;
  alpha = exp(xi_barre + sigma_alpha*alpha_raw);
  // Compute the means mu[j]
  for (j in 1:K) {
    mu[j] = rep_vector(p0,Ndim) + rep_vector(alpha[group[j]]*(t[j]-tau[group[j]]),Ndim) + exp(xi_barre)*compute_delta(delta_d,Kxd,invKd) + compute_A(c,Ns,Ndim)*s[group[j]];
  }
}

model{
  // Distribution of the random effects
  alpha_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  tau_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  for (j in 1:p){
    s[j] ~ normal(rep_vector(0,Ns),1);
  }
  // Likelihood
  for (j in 1:K){
    y[j] ~ normal(mu[j],sigma);
  }
}

The functions 'compute_A' and 'compute_delta' are specific to my problem. I do not think that explaining their role in the model is relevant here. Still, if you want, I can explain more.
The problem I am facing is the following one. I would like to use this STAN code with data which is such that :
* p = 700
* Ndim = 2000
* K = 3147
* Nc = 250
* Ns = 2
but after my code is compiled, I see that more than 40Gb of RAM is used on my computer. Eventually, the processes associated to STAN go into SWAP memory and I have to kill them before my computer freezes.
What am I doing wrong ? Why is this code using so much memory in less than 1 minute ? Overall, the data is approximately 40Mb large, which is not so much (from my point of view).
Is this problem due to because I have many 'transformed parameters' ?

By the way, I am using rstan_2.12.1 with R Version 3.3.2 (2016-10-31) on a Linux machine.

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Why is my code using so much memory ?
parts:
Not sure why the model is using to much memory, but you might try either cmdstan or write the samples to a file rather than memory (sample_file = "your_file_name"). This should reduce the amount of memory being used. Otherwise, you can move parameters you don't need to save into the model block. Lastly, you can discard the warmup (save_warmup = FALSE) to also reduce the size of the samples.

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Why is my code using so much memory ?
parts:
Memory gets used two ways.

Matt Espe outlined the first, which is saving draws in memory.
And it looks like you have a 40K entry matrix, which means 8 bytes
per entry minimum per iteration. So this can add up fast.

The second memory hog is derivative calculations. Stan stores
the entire graph of the expression used to calculate the density and
requires roughly 40 bytes of memory per subexpression computed.

Also, your code can be made more efficient. Things like this:

to_row_vector(auxA)*auxA

would be better written as auxA' * auxA, but we have a built in
dot_self(auxA) function which is more economical in memory and faster.
We also allow scalars to be added to vectors, so instead of

rep_vector(p0,Ndim) + (some Ndim vector)

you can just write

p0 + (some Ndim vector)

We also have an append_row that takes a scalar as an argument
so you don't have to create a 1-element vector.

But even making the program more efficient, those big matrix
multiplications are killers.

- Bob
